item.title: Local woman shares her experience of cancer scare
item.description: A Monaghan woman has shared her experience of having a cancer scare following the discovery of a benign tumour. Orla Sweeney spoke on the Joe Finnegan show this morning, explaining how her symptoms began in August 2024. She started to experience pain in her neck and shoulder, which she dismissed and put down to her job as a hairdresser. Advertisement She went to the physio and doctor but the pain only got worse, and she began to have pains in her chest, shortness of breath and severe headaches.

item.title: Smyth welcomes reopening of China for Irish beef
item.description: A local TD has welcomed the reopening of the Chinese market for Irish beef. The Taoiseach Micheál Martin and the Minister for Agriculture, Martin Heydon, made the announcement yesterday. It follows an announcement by the General Administration of Customs in China (GACC) regarding the reopening of access to the Chinese market for beef produced in Ireland. item.title: Appeal over conviction for Kevin Lunney attack dismissed
item.description: The Court of Appeal has dismissed all challenges to the convictions handed down to three men who kidnapped and tortured Kevin Lunney in September 2019. The director of Quinn Industrial Holdings, which has since been rebranded, was abducted by the gang as he made his way home from work. After his abduction, Kevin Lunney was taken to what he believed to be a horse box in a yard in Co Cavan where he was savagely beaten and doused in bleach. item.title: Cavan CO CO called on to remove portrait of Seán McKiernan from council chamber
item.description: A Sinn Fein Cavan County Councillor is calling on the local authority to remove a photograph of former cathaoirleach Sean McKiernan. The photograph is on display alongside other Cathaoirligh in the Cavan County Council chamber. Cllr Noel Connell has made the call in the aftermath of the former Fine Gael councillor and cathaoirleach waa jailed for two years and nine months for stealing €172,000 from a housing charity. item.title: Residents complimentary about Cavan nursing home staff
item.description: A Co. Cavan nursing home was found to be not compliant with eight regulations of the Health Act 2007. St Joseph's Nursing Home in Lurgan Glebe Virginia received an unannounced inspection on the 24th July 2025. The centre provides 24-hour nursing care to 52 residents who require long and short term care. Advertisement At the time of the inspection there were 43 residents in the centre.
